intro.title: Role-Based Route Protection
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular application that restricts access to certain routes based on a user's role. You will learn how to implement role-based route protection using Angular's built-in router guards. The core programming concept involves creating a custom guard service that checks a user's role before allowing navigation. You will work with TypeScript interfaces to define roles, Angular services to manage authentication state, and the CanActivate interface to secure routes. By the end, you'll have a functional guard that redirects users without the proper role to a safe page.
intro.usecase: Role-based route protection is a foundational security pattern in enterprise web applications. Developers implement it to control user access to different sections of a product, such as an admin dashboard, a customer portal, or internal reporting tools. For example, in a healthcare application, a doctor might see patient records and scheduling panels, while a receptionist only sees appointment forms and contact lists. This ensures users interact only with the UI components and data relevant to their permissions, maintaining security and a streamlined user experience.
